title: Must You Hire a Construction Supervisor for a House in Vietnam? (2026)
desc: Must a private house hire a supervision consultant? 2026 rules under the Construction Law 2025 and Decree 207/2026: when mandatory, scope, penalties.
summary: A private house under 7 floors is only encouraged to have supervision; houses of 7 floors or more, or with 2 or more basements, must organize supervision under Decree 207/2026/ND-CP. The scope of supervision and fines are set out.
body: p

Many homeowners ask: when building a family home yourself, must you hire a supervision firm, or is it enough for the workers to follow the drawings? The answer depends on the size of the house, under Article 56 of the Construction Law 2025 and Article 10 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP (both effective from 1 July 2026).
h2
1. General principle: works must be supervised
p

Under Clause 1, Article 56 of the Construction Law 2025, a construction work must be supervised for quality, quantity, schedule, occupational safety and environmental protection during construction. For private houses of households and individuals, the Law only encourages supervision.
p
The investor may supervise personally or hire a supervision contractor (Article 60). If not doing it personally, a supervision consultant suited to the type and grade of the work must be hired.
h2
2. Private houses: when mandatory and when only encouraged?
p
Under Clause 3, Article 10 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP:
ul

Houses under 7 floors with no more than 1 basement: the owner organizes construction and supervision personally and is responsible for the safety of the work, neighboring works and the environment. Organizing supervision and preparing and keeping records under the Decree is only encouraged.
Houses of 7 floors or more or with 2 or more basements: the owner must organize construction and construction supervision exactly as the Decree 207/2026/ND-CP requires for other works.
p

Even where only encouraged, the homeowner remains responsible if construction causes unsafe conditions or settlement or cracks in the neighboring house. Having a technically knowledgeable supervisor is the most effective way to reduce risk.
h2
3. What does supervision of a private house cover?
p
Under Clause 4, Article 10, the content of construction supervision of a private house includes:
ol
Construction methods and safety measures for the house and adjoining and nearby works.
Quality of construction materials, components and equipment before they are used in construction.
Scaffolding, temporary supporting structures, and construction machinery and equipment.
Safety measures in construction.
p

For houses where it is mandatory, the scope of supervision is broader under Article 20: checking the contractor's capacity, approving materials, checking construction methods, acceptance, confirming quantities and as-built drawings; the supervisor from a consulting organization must have the capacity required by regulations.
h2
4. What qualifications does the supervisor need?
ul

The homeowner must not let an organization or individual without expertise and experience design, build or supervise a private house when the law requires it (Point c, Clause 2, Article 22 of Decree 339/2026/ND-CP).

An individual holding a construction supervision position must have the corresponding supervision practice certificate (Clause 1, Article 88 of the Construction Law 2025; Article 37 of Decree 212/2026/ND-CP).

Supervising finishing work such as plastering, tiling, painting, installing doors and other work that does not affect the load-bearing structure does not require a practice certificate (Clause 3, Article 27).
h2
5. What is the penalty for not organizing supervision?
p
Under Article 22 of Decree 339/2026/ND-CP (effective from 26 August 2026):
ul
Letting a person without expertise and experience design, build or supervise a private house: a fine of VND 20-40 million, plus an order to arrange a suitably qualified person.
Failing to organize construction supervision as required: a fine of VND 60-80 million, plus an order to organize supervision.
Failing to install a project sign at the site entrance: a fine of VND 10-20 million.
p

The levels above apply to organizations; individuals are fined half (Clause 4, Article 5). Homeowners should state clearly in the contract who supervises and what is supervised; see also Conditions to start building a house 2026.
note

This article is only a summary for reference and does not replace the legal documents. From 20 May 2026 to 28 February 2027, Resolution 66.18/2026/NQ-CP on reducing business conditions relates to Clauses 1 and 2, Article 88 of the Construction Law; our legal library does not yet have the full text of this resolution. From 1 March 2027, Clauses 1 and 2, Article 88 are amended by Law 24/2026/QH16 (not yet in force).
